cards.text: Friend, Jesus is teaching in parables, everyday stories with a big truth tucked inside. He puts another one before the people listening. The kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field.
Good seed, good field, good start. Then night comes and everyone is asleep, and you KNOW what that means: something's about to happen nobody signed up for.

cards.question: While everyone is asleep, who sneaks into the man's field?
Out in the man's field, the intruder sows ___ among the wheat.

cards.text: And then he slips away. Sowing weeds and sneaking off is the farm version of the coworker who breaks the copier and quietly walks back to his desk like NOTHING happened.

cards.question: True or false: In the man's field, the weeds show up the very next morning, before the wheat even sprouts.

cards.text: Once the weeds appear, the owner's servants come to him. They ask, “Sir, didn’t you sow good seed in your field? Where then did the weeds come from?”

cards.question: How does the owner answer his servants when they ask where the weeds came from?

cards.text: The servants ask him, “Do you want us to go and pull them up?” I bet those servants already have their sleeves rolled up and are READY to go, friend.

cards.question: True or false: The owner tells his servants to go pull up the weeds right away.
Why doesn't the owner want his servants pulling up the weeds now?

answers.text: They might uproot the wheat too
The weeds will die on their own
The servants need to rest first

cards.text: So the owner says, “Let both grow together until the harvest.” Friend, I waited YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, so this man has my full respect.

cards.question: At harvest time, the owner will have the harvesters collect the ___ first, then gather the ___ into his barn.
What does the owner say will happen to the weeds once they're tied in bundles?

answers.text: They will be sold at market

cards.text: Jesus puts another parable before them. The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that a man took and planted in his field.
Jesus says it is the smallest of all seeds. Friend, I drop ONE sprinkle on my bakery floor and it's gone FOREVER, so imagine planting something that small and expecting anything.

cards.question: Jesus says the smallest of all seeds grows into the largest of garden plants. What does that mustard plant become?
True or false: The mustard plant gets so big that the birds of the air come and nest in its branches.

cards.text: He tells them still another parable, and this one has a woman with three measures of flour. NOW you're in my department, friend, because I'm a cookie man and I KNOW dough.

cards.question: Jesus says the kingdom of heaven is like ___ that a woman mixed into three measures of flour.
Once the woman mixes the leaven in, how much of the flour ends up leavened?

cards.text: Weeds, a seed, some leaven: BOOM, BOOM, BOOM, three parables back to back. Then the story steps back to tell us how Jesus is teaching the crowds.

cards.question: True or false: When Jesus teaches the crowds here, He tells them some things without using a parable.

cards.text: Friend, even this way of teaching was spoken of long before. It fulfills what was spoken through the prophet: “I will open My mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden since the foundation of the world.”
Then Jesus dismisses the crowds and goes into the house. His disciples come to Him with a request.

cards.question: Which parable do the disciples ask Jesus to explain?

cards.text: And Jesus explains it, piece by piece. Friend, I shared that junk drawer with a stack of old instruction manuals, and not ONE of them ever explained anything this clearly.

cards.question: In the parable of the weeds, who does Jesus say is the One who sows the good seed?
In Jesus' explanation, the field is the ___.

cards.text: The Son of Man is a name Jesus uses for Himself, so HE'S the one sowing. And the good seed represents the sons of the kingdom, the crop every farmer is rooting for, friend.

cards.question: In Jesus' explanation, who are the weeds?

answers.text: The sons of the evil one

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says the enemy who sowed the weeds is the devil.

cards.text: Remember, in the parable everything waits until the harvest. Now Jesus says what the harvest is, and who's doing the harvesting.

cards.question: Jesus says the harvest is the end of the ___, and the harvesters are ___.

cards.text: Now Jesus gets serious, friend: “As the weeds are collected and burned in the fire, so will it be at the end of the age.” And He says the Son of Man will send out His angels.

cards.question: What will the Son of Man's angels weed out of His kingdom?

answers.text: Every cause of sin and all who practice lawlessness
Every worry and all who live in fear
Every field that never bore any grain

cards.text: Jesus says, “And they will throw them into the fiery furnace, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.” Friend, I'm setting my jokes down for this one, because Jesus means every word.

cards.question: After all that, what does Jesus say the righteous will do in the kingdom of their Father?

cards.text: Jesus ends with, “He who has ears, let him hear.” And He's not done teaching about the kingdom yet, friend, so keep both ears open.

findings.problem: The opening card spends words defining "parables" ("everyday stories with a big truth tucked inside"). Hard words are left to the dictionary pop-up.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: "Then night comes" adds a time the text doesn't give. Matthew 13:25 says only "while everyone was asleep."

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The card mostly recaps the three parables ("Weeds, a seed, some leaven: BOOM, BOOM, BOOM") and tells nothing from Matthew 13:34, the verse it cites. Its only other line is a vague setup.
Multiple choice takes 5 of the stop's 8 choice cards (cards 2, 4, 7, 12 and 14). Fill in the blank has 2 and true or false has 1, so one type dominates by a wide margin.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: "The Son of Man is a name Jesus uses for Himself" is a fact from outside the passage. Matthew 13:37-38 doesn't say it, and the card gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: "Every field that never bore any grain" is not the same kind of thing as the other answers, which are causes and people. It is also much easier to rule out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
